name: The Water Tower's grounds
address: West of Pine Street between Chicago Avenue and Pearson Street, North Side

status.text: Its railing stood through the fire
status.today: The park round the Water Tower
status.note: The railing still stands in a photograph taken after the fire. The grounds are a park today.

built.note: Laid out with the water works, begun in 1867.

summary: The open lawn round the Water Tower, with shrub beds, young trees and walks. No houses stood between the tower and Chicago Avenue. A stone kerb with an iron railing ran round it.

key.label: In the middle
key.value: The Water Tower, which survived the fire

notable.text: An 1866-67 print shows the tower standing alone on open, planted ground.
How far the grounds reached is taken from today's park round the tower.
notable.note: No survey of the 1860s lot was found; a photograph of about 1890 shows the same fenced lawn.

story.text: The fire sweeps past. The tower and its railing stand; the grass and young trees burn.
story.note: A photograph taken after the fire shows the tower and its railing still standing. The grass and trees around them are burnt.
